ecological_question: Does anthropogenic redistribution of larval host plants disproportionately expand geographic resource opportunity for butterflies with broader taxonomic host breadth?

source_panel.resource_eligible_definition: host_family_count > 0 and native host-resource WGSRPD3 unit count > 0

resource_geography.contemporary_envelope: extinct=0, location_doubtful=0, native and introduced both retained

primary_descriptive_association.inference: exploratory descriptive; no confirmatory alpha or decision

completeness_sensitivity.lower_bound_subset: resolved HOSTS-WCVP host-species count >= LepTraits NumberOfHostplantFamilies

additional_descriptive: Spearman host-family breadth vs introduced-added units
Spearman resolved host-species count vs log resource expansion
Spearman native resource breadth vs log resource expansion
host-breadth-stratum medians for native, contemporary, added, ratio and introduced share
descriptive least-squares model: log resource expansion ~ log1p(host-family count) + log1p(native resource units) + log1p(resolved host species)
